title: Residue-transcendence pullback of dimension functions
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian universally catenary scheme: every affine coordinate ring is Noetherian and every finite-type algebra over it is catenary, in the sense spelled out in [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $f:T\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A dimension function here means an integer-valued function whose value drops by one at each immediate specialization of geometric points, as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. If $\delta_S$ is a dimension function on $S$, then
$$\delta_T(t)=\delta_S(f(t))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(t))}\kappa(t)$$
is a dimension function on $T$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 02JW, lemma-dimension-function-propagates; ILO XIV, Corollary 2.5.2 (with residue-field order as in its proof)

proof.text: The claim is local around the specialized point. Fix a specialization $a\rightsquigarrow b$ in $T$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $f(b)$ and, from the affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $b$ mapping to $V$, with $B$ finite type over $A$. Every open containing a point contains its generalizations, so $a\in U$ and $f(a)\in V$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by the hypothesis; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] give that $T$ is locally Noetherian and $B$ is Noetherian. The ring $B$ is universally catenary: a finite type $B$-algebra is finite type over $A$ (combine the two finite lists of generators), hence catenary by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Thus $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ are Noetherian schemes covered by a single affine open whose ring is universally catenary, which is exactly the universal-catenarity hypothesis of [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion](b). Strict localizations at geometric points of $U$ (resp. $V$) are the same whether taken in $U$ or in $T$ (resp. in $V$ or in $S$): a pointed etale neighbourhood in $U$ is one in $T$, and for a pointed etale neighbourhood $W$ in $T$ the open $W\times_TU$ is one in $U$ mapping to $W$, so the neighbourhoods over $U$ are initial in the limit of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Hence geometric specializations between points of a chart, and their immediacy, are the same on the chart and on the scheme. Consequently [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion] applies on these charts to both the input and output geometric immediate-specialization conditions.

source.place: Tag 02JW, lemma-dimension-function-propagates, first affine reduction; ILO XIV Proposition 2.1.4

proof.text: The displayed formula is integer-valued. For any $t\in U$, put $s=f(t)$. The affine fibre ring $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(s)$ is finite type over $\kappa(s)$: images of a finite list of algebra generators of $B$ still generate after tensoring [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The point of this fibre over $t$ has local ring $\mathcal O_{U,t}/\mathfrak m_s\mathcal O_{U,t}$ by [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient]; its residue field is $\kappa(t)$, since the quotient ideal lies in the maximal ideal and quotienting once more by that maximal ideal gives $\mathcal O_{U,t}/\mathfrak m_t$. Apply [lem-kun-finite-type-residue-trdeg] to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $\kappa(s)$. It gives $e_t=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)<\infty$. Thus $\delta_T(t)=\delta_S(s)+e_t$ is an integer. Here and below the residue fields on an affine chart are those of the original scheme, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization, def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 02JW, definition of delta_{X/S}; finiteness of the residue transcendence degrees

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q_1$ be the primes of $B$ corresponding to $a,b$, and put $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak q_i\cap A$. Set $R=A/\mathfrak p_0$ and $D=B/\mathfrak q_0$. These are domains and the induced map $R\to D$ is injective: its kernel is $\mathfrak q_0\cap A$ modulo $\mathfrak p_0$. The images of the generators of $B/A$ generate $D/R$. A quotient of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian (lift an ideal to the original ring and descend its finitely many generators). Moreover $R$ and $D$ are universally catenary: every finite type algebra over either quotient is finite type over $A$, hence catenary by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. The reduced point closures on the charts are $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}D$; their generic points are $f(a)$ and $a$. The scheme-to-ring residue identifications are given by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification]. Quotienting by the generic-point primes leaves all residue fields of points in these closures unchanged: at a prime $\mathfrak r$ containing the quotient ideal the field is $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak r)$, or $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak r)$, as in [lem-exc-dimension-formula-universally-catenary-finite-type-domain]. Write $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_1/\mathfrak p_0$ in $R$ and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q_1/\mathfrak q_0$ in $D$, and put $h_S=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$ and $h_T=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$.

source.place: Tag 02JW, reduction to the reduced closures of the general points

proof.text: Choose a saturated chain from $0$ to $\mathfrak p$ in $R$. By the catenary condition expanded in [def-exc-excellent-ring], the lengths of chains between these endpoints are bounded and all saturated chains have the same length. A chain of largest length exists, is saturated, and has length $h_S$: any chain ending at $\mathfrak p$ extends downwards to $0$ and can be saturated. Lift this chain to primes of $A$ between $\mathfrak p_0$ and $\mathfrak p_1$. Every adjacent pair is an immediate specialization on $V$: a point between the endpoints would give a prime strictly between consecutive primes. More explicitly, [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] applied to the reduced closure of the general endpoint says that the local dimension at the special endpoint is $1$, since its generalization chains have maximum length $1$. Since $V$ is Noetherian and universally catenary (Step 1), the final clause of [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion] makes each such pair an immediate specialization in the sense of the definition, that is, the pair of underlying points of an immediate geometric specialization of $V$, hence of $S$ by Step 1; by its part (a) every geometric specialization over the pair is immediate. The dimension-function paragraph of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex] defines immediacy by dimension one of the reduced closure in the strict localization and requires $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ at each such specialization. These equations for $\delta_S$ add along this chain to give $\delta_S(f(a))-\delta_S(f(b))=h_S$. If $\mathfrak p=0$, the chain is empty and the equality is $0=0$. This is the finite telescoping-chain argument underlying Topology Tag 02IA, not an additional lemma taken without proof.

source.place: Tag 02JW, cancellation of the base dimension difference; Topology Tag 02IA, lemma-dimension-function-catenary, finite-chain argument

proof.text:
Apply [lem-exc-dimension-formula-universally-catenary-finite-type-domain] to $R\subset D$ and $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$. Step 3 verifies every hypothesis, including universal catenarity of the Noetherian domain $R$ and finite type of the inclusion. Its equality is
$$h_T+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(b))}\kappa(b)=h_S+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(a))}\kappa(a).$$
Indeed the fraction fields of $R,D$ are the residue fields at their generic points, identified with $\kappa(f(a)),\kappa(a)$ in Step 3. Subtracting the finite integers of Step 2 and using Step 4 yields
$$\delta_T(a)-\delta_T(b)=h_S+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(a))}\kappa(a)-\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(b))}\kappa(b)=h_T.$$
If $a\ne b$, then $\mathfrak q\ne0$ and $0\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ gives $h_T\ge1$. If $a\rightsquigarrow b$ is geometric immediate, [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion](b) on $U$ gives $\dim\mathcal O_{\overline{\{a\}}_{\mathrm{red}},b}=1$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] this is $h_T$, since both are the supremum of prime-chain lengths from $0$ to $\mathfrak q$ in $D$. Hence the difference is exactly $1$. Thus $\delta_T(a)=\delta_T(b)+1$ for each immediate geometric specialization, exactly the dimension-function paragraph of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. This holds on every chart and therefore on $T$; it also proves the strict decrease required by the usual Zariski convention.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q22-10d12a277 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and its five steps in full, all 18 cited statements, Stacks 02JW (morphisms.tex, lemma-dimension-function-propagates, statement and whole proof) and ILO XIV 2.1.3–2.1.8 and 2.5.1–2.5.2 (pp. 209–211, 216). The statement is 02JW with the geometric dimension-function notion. It is true, uses the residue-field order of the proof of 2.5.2, and adds or weakens nothing. I tested it on the identity, A^1/k, a finite map, a DVR and a specialization inside one fibre. The arithmetic in Steps 2, 3 and 5 is correct: fibre trdeg is finite, the domain reduction is valid, and the 02IJ equality gives delta_T(a)-delta_T(b)=h_T with the right sign. No new nodes, no cycle, no SGA citation. The corrected item is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/; it repairs three faults. (1) Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-universally-catenary-affine-cover (Stacks 02J9) is generic commutative algebra, not a trace-formula or Poincaré step, and it is not needed. The item's hypothesis already makes A universally catenary, B is shown directly, and criterion (b) only needs a cover by universally catenary affine opens, which U=Spec B is. I removed it from Step 1, proof_deps and tool_uses. (2) Step 1 justified that the strict localization does not change on an open chart by 'the local ring is unchanged'. In this DAG the strict localization is defined as a limit over étale neighbourhoods, so I replaced this with the cofinality argument and cited def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit. (3) Step 4 cited only part (a) of lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion, which is vacuous unless a geometric specialization over the pair exists. It now uses the criterion's final clause on the universally catenary Noetherian chart V. The closure still reaches three generic trf nodes (ind-étale strict-local invariance, bounded-below derived adjunction, henselian integral algebra), but only through the existing criterion's stmt_deps; none is part of the assumed statements. Accepted tool_uses: the eight remaining generic nodes.
